All error statements here are historical acquisition-time errors; current candidate predictions remain unmeasured.","batch_rationale":"The 32 experiments form interpretable local comparisons across the supplied pool, where the selected molecules are already represented and missing relationships are primarily conditional. Direct follow-up on m53 and m56 tests whether recent large weak-eluent corrections transfer across loading and between solvent boundaries. The m72 design separates reproduction of a strong-condition reference from pure-EA loading response and a missing solvent bridge; the m92 repeat similarly checks an influential loading association before extending its curve. Six nitrogen-base experiments provide three matched pure-EA-to-1/1 comparisons, allowing retraining to learn scaffold-dependent strong responses rather than a common offset. The six malonate experiments probe substitution and loading in a chemically prevalent family with sharply different recorded responses. Strong anchors and transition labels for m128, m28, m180 and m197 constrain carbonyl and donor-containing environments without assuming that one response shape generalizes across them. The m185 comparison tests a specific unusual prediction, and the m0 pair plus m4 bridge extend coverage to nonpolar aromatic graphs whose baselines should not be dictated by polar-scaffold failures. Multiple selections on a molecule serve explicit loading, response-shape or reproducibility questions. These labels may improve accuracy across the Row-distribution by constraining relationships shared by many remaining rows, rather than by maximizing selected retention volumes. CW distance is supplementary coverage evidence, and single-predictor quantile spans are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. V2 minus V1 remains an elution interval; loading mass is the recorded density-times-volume feature. Missing experimental factors limit causal interpretation. All 32 distinct selected IDs and their exact supplied premeasurement predictions are frozen through this packet before any new label reveal."}
